findings.title: 63 MB of cargo build artifacts (target/) shipped inside /output, with no .gitignore, and they are already stale
findings.why_it_is_wrong: Requirement 5 asks for a "complete Cargo project" in /output; target/ is build output, not project source. Three concrete problems: (1) /output/target/release/test18 (md5 0bb4cd1b4574d539dbe086b5d430128d) is stale -- it was built from the pre-refactor buckets.rs and no longer corresponds to the shipped sources or to /output/test18 (md5 93a01d0f62600b6a49ec044338766c11). (2) /output/target/.rustc_info.json and the .fingerprint files hard-code the absolute path /output, so the artifacts are machine-specific despite the sources being fully relocatable. (3) There is no .gitignore, so a naive commit or archive of the deliverable carries all 63 MB and the stale binary along with it. The correctness of the deliverable is unaffected -- I confirmed a source edit still triggers a rebuild -- but the shipped tree contains a binary that does not match its own sources.
findings.concrete_trigger: `cp -r /output /tmp/copy2 && cd /tmp/copy2 && cargo build --release` prints `Fresh test18 v1.0.0 (/tmp/copy2)` and `Finished release [optimized] target(s) in 0.01s` -- cargo performs no compilation at all and hands back the artifact fingerprinted for a different directory. Separately, `md5sum /output/target/release/test18 /output/test18` shows the two disagree (0bb4cd1b... vs 93a01d0f...), and only the latter reflects the current sortedcontainers/buckets.rs.

findings.title: Module-wide `#![allow(dead_code, unused_imports)]` silences four real warnings, one of which is a genuinely unused re-export
findings.why_it_is_wrong: The attribute is documented and scoped to the sortedcontainers module (compat.rs and test18.rs are not covered), so the "clean build in every configuration" result is partly purchased with a blanket allow rather than earned. It also covers buckets.rs, cursor.rs and sorted_map.rs wholesale, so any future accidental dead code or stray import in the container modules will be silenced too. `pub use self::cursor::Cursor;` on line 20 is a re-export nothing consumes -- test18.rs imports only `update` and `SortedMap` -- and the unused-import warning for it is a true positive, not merely unexercised library API. A narrower `#[allow(dead_code)]` on the impl blocks, plus deleting the dead re-export, would keep the build clean without the blanket suppression.
findings.concrete_trigger: Copy the tree to /tmp, delete line 15 of sortedcontainers/mod.rs, then `rustc --edition 2021 test18.rs -o /tmp/out` emits exactly: `warning: unused import: \`self::cursor::Cursor\`` (mod.rs:19:9 post-deletion, i.e. line 20 in the shipped file); `warning: method \`get_mut\` is never used` (buckets.rs:142:12); `warning: methods \`is_end\` and \`entry\` are never used` (cursor.rs:29:12); `warning: methods \`get\`, \`get_mut\`, and \`end\` are never used` (sorted_map.rs:58:12); `warning: 4 warnings emitted`.

findings.title: Shipped package metadata cites a source path `tests/test18.cpp` that exists nowhere
findings.why_it_is_wrong: `description = "Pure-std Rust port of tests/test18.cpp and the sortedcontainers C++ header"` and the crate-root doc comment at /output/test18.rs:1 (`//! Port of \`tests/test18.cpp\``) both name a relative path that resolves to nothing from /output or from the workspace root. The actual C++ original is /workspace/dataset/test18.cpp. This is baked into `cargo metadata` output and into any rustdoc build, so a reader following the reference finds nothing.
findings.concrete_trigger: `ls -d /output/tests /workspace/tests` -> both `No such file or directory`, while `grep -n 'tests/test18.cpp' /output/Cargo.toml /output/test18.rs` matches Cargo.toml:6 and test18.rs:1.
